metadata.coordinate_system: Selenographic latitude and longitude in degrees

priority_scale.meaning: 1 is always eligible for display; 20 is shown only at the closest zoom levels
priority_scale.note: Priority is a label-density/zoom-culling rank, not scientific importance.

metadata.image_note: image.filename is relative to the Images directory. Keep the Images folder beside this JSON. Failed downloads are marked with download_error.
metadata.image_source: NASA Image and Video Library, with Wikimedia Commons fallback

craters.name: Tycho
craters.description: A prominent, relatively young impact crater known for its bright ray system, which extends across much of the lunar surface. Its terraced walls and central peak are especially striking.

image.alt: NASA image: The Floor of Tycho Crater

craters.name: Copernicus
craters.description: A large, relatively young impact crater with terraced walls, a central mountain complex, and an extensive system of bright ejecta rays.

image.alt: NASA image: Limb of Copernicus Impact Crater

craters.name: Aristarchus
craters.description: One of the brightest large craters on the Moon. It lies on the Aristarchus Plateau and is surrounded by bright ejecta.

image.alt: NASA image: Multispectral Mosaic of the Aristarchus Crater and Plateau

craters.name: Plato
craters.description: A distinctive crater with a relatively dark, smooth basalt-covered floor that contrasts with the surrounding highlands.

image.alt: NASA image: Plato Crater

craters.name: Clavius
craters.description: One of the largest craters on the near side. Its eroded rim and chain of overlapping craters record a long history of impacts.

image.alt: NASA image: Swooping over the Lunar Highlands

craters.name: Kepler
craters.description: A relatively young crater with bright rays and a rugged ejecta blanket extending across Oceanus Procellarum.

image.alt: NASA image: ATV 2 Johannes Kepler docked

craters.name: Grimaldi
craters.description: An ancient impact structure with a dark basaltic floor near the western limb.

image.alt: NASA image: Capture My Good Side –The Moon

craters.name: Schickard
craters.description: A large ancient crater in the southwestern highlands. Its floor contains dark deposits and numerous smaller craters.

image.alt: Wikipedia article image for Schickard

craters.name: Aristoteles
craters.description: A prominent northern crater with terraced inner walls and a rugged floor.

image.alt: Wikipedia article image for Aristoteles

craters.name: Theophilus
craters.description: A well-preserved crater with a central mountain complex and terraced walls. It partly overlaps the older crater Cyrillus.

image.alt: NASA image: Oblique view of crater Theophilus at northwest edge of Sea of Nectar

craters.name: Ptolemaeus
craters.description: A large, ancient walled plain with a relatively level floor marked by many small craterlets.

image.alt: NASA image: Apollo 12 Lunar Module, in landing configuration, photographed in lunar orbit

craters.name: Alphonsus
craters.description: An ancient crater between Ptolemaeus and Arzachel, notable for dark-halo deposits and volcanic features.

image.alt: NASA image: Lunar Reconaissance Orbiter photo of Alphonsus crater

craters.name: Arzachel
craters.description: A well-defined crater south of Alphonsus with terraced walls and a prominent central peak.

image.alt: Wikipedia article image for Arzachel

craters.name: Gassendi
craters.description: A complex crater on the northern edge of Mare Humorum, with a fractured floor and central peaks.

image.alt: Wikipedia article image for Gassendi

craters.name: Langrenus
craters.description: A prominent eastern near-side crater with a rugged central peak complex and terraced walls.

image.alt: NASA image: View of near full Moon photographed by Apollo 13 during transearth journey

craters.name: Petavius
craters.description: A large crater with a fractured floor and a prominent rille extending from its central mountain.

image.alt: Wikipedia article image for Petavius

craters.name: Piccolomini
craters.description: A southern highlands crater with a well-preserved rim and central peak.

image.alt: Wikipedia article image for Piccolomini

craters.name: Endymion

image.alt: Wikipedia article image for Endymion

craters.name: Posidonius

craters.name: Plinius

image.alt: Wikipedia article image for Plinius

craters.name: Thebit

image.alt: Wikipedia article image for Thebit

image.alt: Wikipedia article image for Wargentin

craters.name: Bailly

image.alt: Wikipedia article image for Bailly

craters.name: Atlas

craters.name: Moltke

craters.name: Hind

maria.name: Mare Imbrium
maria.description: One of the largest impact basins on the near side. It was flooded by ancient basaltic lava, creating broad, relatively smooth dark plains.

image.alt: NASA image: ARC-1990-A91-2011

maria.name: Mare Tranquillitatis
maria.description: The Sea of Tranquility is a large basaltic plain and the historic Apollo 11 landing region.

image.alt: NASA image: Rima Ariadaeus - A Linear Rille

maria.name: Mare Serenitatis
maria.description: The Sea of Serenity is a large volcanic basin with smooth basaltic plains and complex surrounding mountain structures.

image.alt: NASA image: Aratus CA

maria.name: Mare Crisium
maria.description: The Sea of Crises is a distinctive, nearly circular impact basin on the northeastern near side.

image.alt: NASA image: Soviet Union Lunar Sample Return Missions

maria.name: Oceanus Procellarum
maria.description: The Ocean of Storms is the largest expanse of lunar basaltic plains, covering much of the western near side.

image.alt: NASA image: A “Handprint” on the Moon

maria.name: Mare Nubium
maria.description: The Sea of Clouds is an ancient basaltic plain in the southern near side.

maria.name: Mare Fecunditatis
maria.description: The Sea of Fertility is a large basaltic plain in the southeastern near side.

image.alt: NASA image: Luna 16

maria.name: Mare Nectaris

maria.name: Mare Humorum

image.alt: Wikipedia article image for Mare Vaporum

image.alt: Wikipedia article image for Mare Australe

image.alt: Wikipedia article image for Mare Spumans

image.alt: Wikipedia article image for Mare Undarum

maria.name: Mare Cognitum

landing_sites.name: Apollo 11
landing_sites.description: Historic landing site of Apollo 11 on July 20, 1969, in Mare Tranquillitatis. Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first humans to walk on the Moon.

image.alt: NASA image: Summer Moon Festival, Wapakoneta, Ohio, Apollo 11 Moon Landin...

landing_sites.name: Chang'e 4 / Yutu-2

image.alt: Related lunar image for Chang'e 4 / Yutu-2; no dedicated lead image was available on its Wikipedia page

landing_sites.description: Landing site in Von Kármán crater within the South Pole–Aitken Basin. Chang'e 4 achieved the first soft landing on the lunar far side and deployed the Yutu-2 rover.

impact_basins.name: South Pole / Aitken Basin

image.alt: Related lunar image for South Pole–Aitken Basin; no dedicated lead image was available on its Wikipedia page

impact_basins.description: One of the largest and oldest known impact basins in the Solar System. It dominates much of the lunar southern far side and exposes deep crustal materials.

impact_basins.name: Hertzsprung Basin

image.alt: NASA image: Vavilov Crater Along the Hertzsprung Basin Rim

impact_basins.description: A large multi-ring impact basin on the far side, with a complex structure modified by later impacts.

impact_basins.name: Apollo Basin

image.alt: NASA image: Swoon at the Moon

impact_basins.description: A large double-ring impact basin within the South Pole Aitken region. China's Chang'e 6 landing area lies within this basin.

impact_basins.name: Mendel-Rydberg Basin

image.alt: Wikipedia article image for Mendel-Rydberg Basin

impact_basins.description: A large degraded basin near the southwestern limb, with remnants of its ancient ring structure.
